findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1747 is the "Splunk Add-on for Cisco WSA" (Splunk_TA_cisco-wsa); the REST API Modular Input is Splunkbase 1546 (rest_ta). The same wrong ID appears in `references` ("REST API Modular Input on Splunkbase (1747)") and in `detailedImplementation` ("Install **REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase 1747)**"), so readers would install the wrong package.
findings.quote: using **REST API Modular Input** (**Splunkbase app ID 1747**)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 1747 with 1546 in dataSources, references and detailedImplementation, and point the reference URL to https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1546.

findings.explanation: The HashiCorp Vault tag comes from the generic phrase "credential vaulting" / "external vault". This UC monitors badge access controllers (for example Lenel, CCURE, AMAG, HID), not HashiCorp Vault, so it will appear in the wrong equipment filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove hashicorp / hashicorp_vault. Tag the physical access-control equipment slugs used by sibling badge UCs, or leave the field empty if no slug exists.

findings.explanation: `edit_alert_actions` is a system-wide, privileged capability. It lets a role edit all alert actions regardless of ACLs, and it cannot be limited to particular saved searches. Recommending it for a least-privilege physical-security role contradicts the stated intent.
findings.quote: `physical_security_alert_manager` with `schedule_search` + `edit_alert_actions` limited to the UC saved searches
findings.suggested_fix: Grant `schedule_search` and scope it with app/object permissions (write access on the UC saved searches only). Do not grant `edit_alert_actions`, which Splunk says to assign only to privileged roles.

findings.explanation: `implementation` and `visualization` ("sorted by denied attempts") describe after-hours, tailgating and denied-attempt alerting. The `spl` only runs `stats count by badge_holder, door, action | sort -count` over every action, with no time-of-day, denial or threshold logic, so it is an audit report, not an alert.
findings.quote: throttle tailgating duplicates with `stats`/`dedup`, and wire alert actions so physical-security tier-two receives after-hours cage entries
findings.suggested_fix: Present the UC as an audit report showing access-event volume by holder, door and action. Move the after-hours, tailgating and denial alerting to the sibling UCs that implement it (UC-15.3.2, UC-15.3.3, UC-15.3.14), or note the SPL filters such a human would need to add.

findings.explanation: The text describes ingestion over syslog or a REST poller only; no step uses HEC. The references also cite no access-control vendor documentation (for example Lenel OnGuard or CCURE event export) even though the repository guide documents a DB Connect path to `lnl_event_log`.
findings.quote: "title": "Splunk Docs — Send HTTP Event Collector data to Splunk Enterprise"
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the HEC reference, or add HEC as an ingest option. Add vendor event-export documentation or the DB Connect (Splunkbase 2686) path from docs/guides/datacenter-physical.md.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: API RP 1164 3rd edition clause 5.3 appears twice, under regulation "api-rp-1164" and under "API RP 1164", with the same obligationRef. Remove the duplicate entry.

HIPAA Privacy Rule §164.502(a) governs uses and disclosures of PHI, not facility access. A physical access-control audit maps to Security Rule §164.310(a)(1) (facility access controls) and §164.310(a)(2)(iii) (access control and validation procedures). The current mapping overstates relevance; re-map to §164.310 under the HIPAA Security regulation.

Check that TSA SD02C §III.A (cybersecurity implementation plan) and API RP 1164 3rd ed. §5.3 actually name physical access-control event auditing. Also confirm the clause URLs resolve (https://www.tsa.gov/sd02c). Every entry is still marked "Auto-drafted — SME review required" while mode is "satisfies".
A badge access audit with monitoringType Compliance and a CIM Authentication mapping is a Security-pillar UC. Siblings UC-15.3.34 and UC-15.3.35 use Security, but this UC uses "Observability".

The cimSpl splits by `Authentication.src`, but the door or reader (the most useful dimension in the raw SPL) would normally map to `Authentication.dest`. As written, cimSpl does not reproduce the door breakdown in `spl`.

summary: The ingest and implementation prose is more concrete than most siblings. However, it repeatedly names Splunkbase 1747 as the REST API Modular Input when 1747 is the Cisco WSA add-on, it tags HashiCorp Vault as equipment, and its RBAC advice misdescribes `edit_alert_actions`. The compliance block duplicates API RP 1164 and maps a physical-access audit to a HIPAA Privacy Rule clause about PHI disclosures.
